newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Finland says fulfils all EMU criteria.
newsitem.headline: Finland says fulfils all EMU criteria.

text.p: Finnish Finance Minister Sauli Niinisto said on Monday that Finland was now fulfilling all of the criteria for Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) following Saturday's decision to link the markka to the exchange rate mechanism (ERM).
"We are now fulfilling all the criteria," he told a news conference at an EU finance ministers meeting in Luxembourg.
Explaining why Finland had decided to join the currency grid, Niinisto said it had become more obvious since last Spring that a formal ERM link was a criterion for the third phase of EMU.
He said the decision would bring even more stability to the Finnish economy as well as more confidence.
"We are quite satisfied with the rate," he said. Finland joined the ERM at a central rate of 3.04 to the German mark.
Niinisto also said that Finland had had no contacts with other EU countries about joining the ERM at the same time.
There had been speculation that Italy had contacted Finland to coordinate a joint entry into the ERM.
But Niinisto said the timing of Finland's move was not linked to "any ideas outside Finland".
"We had no such contacts with any other member country about joining together," he said.
